correctness.rationale: The complete source proposition and proof were reconstructed from the open preprint. The diagonal operator K is bounded with nonclosed range; Kf_n=e_n makes every transformed weave an orthonormal basis and hence a K-frame. The test vectors x_N=e_N/N lie in R(K*) and force the original upper-frame ratio to equal N^2. The closed-range repair follows directly from the bounded Moore--Penrose inverse and was checked in both directions with explicit constants.

value.rationale: Proposition 2.5 is advertised as a necessary-and-sufficient characterization connecting ordinary wovenness on an operator range with K-wovenness of image sequences. The counterexample shows that one half of this characterization can fail maximally at the Bessel upper bound even though every transformed weave is an orthonormal basis. The repair is structural and quantitative: closed range is exactly what makes minimum-norm preimages uniformly controlled, yielding explicit bounds in both directions.
